case_data.title: Café AI
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
Café AI is a public movement which aims to promote a shared, accessible, and democratic culture around artificial intelligence and digital technologies. Our mission is to empower individuals to make informed and conscious decisions about their individual and collective uses of AI and digital technologies, whether they choose to adopt them, adapt them, or limit their presence in their lives.

Launched in France in 2024 on the request of President Macron by the French National Digital Council (Conseil national du numérique), the movement is today by an independent state project, the Mission Café AI (Mission Café IA), hosted by the Directorate General of Enterprises (Direction générale des entreprises) of the Ministry of the Economy and Finance (Ministère de l’économie et des finances).

Café AI is above all a space for discussion, where individuals can learn, experiment, and debate as part of a shared digital culture. We work with our team of over 1000 volunteers, digital mediation professionals, and professional structures to launch discussion spaces across France, and increasingly across Europe. Alongside this, we propose a large number of activities, games, learning modules and editorial resources enabling citizens to understand better digital technologies. We work to ensure that citizens have the tools they need to make enlightened decisions about their own - and collective - uses of AI and digital technologies. 

We are aiming to involve 2 million French citizens by the end of 2027.
case_data.headline-findings:
No final report as project is ongoing, but the team identify the following areas which have often arisen in the group discussions that we have been a part of:
- Popular fear around AI, not just from elderly participants, but also including the (very) young. Often linked to a perceived lack of regulation, control, and its impact on our society.
- Distrust of being marketed/"forced" to use AI solutions.
- Policies which are perceived to be lacking in environmental protection, such as the construction of data centres, as well as the impact of AI on our information (elections...).
case_data.inclusion-efforts:
Work with civil society groups and existing digital mediation professionals to ensure that as wide a range of citizens as possible are included. The movement is horizontal and decentralised, so data collection on participant numbers and characteristics is limited and often depends on local organisers. Some Cafés are centrally logged - and those upcoming are available on our website [www.cafeia.org/carte-interactive](http://www.cafeia.org/carte-interactive). 

We believe Café AI is unique and important as it works to ensure that citizens' voices are included in decisions and policies about AI and digital technologies, through increasing understanding and creating the opportunities for citizens to discuss the issues together.

As a part of this, we have worked hard to ensure that Cafés are held across France, including outside of major cities and in France's overseas territories (the DOM-TOMs). We work with a number of different civil society groups to tailor Cafés to particular publics, notably for young and elderly people, those with disabilities, and those from areas which are often ignored in digital policy discussions.

Our methods are focused on boosting skills and involvement in dialogue - anyone can run a Café AI, without being an expert, as long as they can ensure the discussion remains respectful, welcoming, and that they do not express a particular position (eg promoting AI). Our resources, designed with communities to foster debate, are freely available and shareable, downloadable from our website.  We have also worked with those interested in other countries to establish sister movements - the format is reproducible freely and open to all. The movement is also frugal, centred on a small-group discussion and simple activities - it is low-cost and easy to implement. Finally, the format is extremely flexible, working equally well in a school, hospital, mountain-top, or in the heart of a large business or government entity.
